project.name: ReGenCity Indonesia
project.descriptor: Urban energy recovery and flexibility platform

pilotGeography.name: North Jakarta
pilotGeography.label: provisional pilot geography

hero.title: Recover what the city already moves.
hero.body: ReGenCity connects port, transit, and water systems that already move mass, vehicles, or pressure. It captures energy that would otherwise be dissipated, uses it locally first, stores the surplus, and coordinates a bounded response when the grid needs flexibility.

problem.title: Urban systems lose useful energy during normal work.
problem.body: Trains brake, cranes lower loads, and water networks reduce pressure as part of their required service. Those events are often treated as losses. ReGenCity treats them as recovery opportunities while keeping transport, cargo, and water service as hard constraints.

cards.title: Braking
cards.body: Electric rail can route regenerative braking energy to another load or a nearby storage node.

cards.title: Lowering
cards.body: Crane lowering cycles can operate the motor-generator in regeneration and share power within the facility.

cards.title: Pressure reduction
cards.body: A suitable pressure-reduction point can use a pump-as-turbine or microturbine while maintaining the required service pressure.

operatingPrinciple.title: Recovery first. Coordination second.
operatingPrinciple.body: The digital layer does not command infrastructure to move wastefully. It forecasts normal operations, routes recovered energy to the nearest useful load, stores the surplus, and dispatches only the flexibility that remains available after safety and service reserves are protected.

steps.title: Normal operations create recovery events
steps.body: A train brakes, a crane lowers a load, or water passes through a suitable pressure-reduction point.

steps.title: Use recovered energy locally
steps.body: The first destination is a nearby accelerating train, lifting crane, station load, or facility load.

steps.title: Store the surplus
steps.body: Supercapacitors, batteries, flywheels, or water and ballast systems absorb energy that cannot be used immediately.

steps.title: Dispatch within operational bounds
steps.body: The coordinator offers stored energy or flexible demand only after local operating limits and reserve requirements are checked.

architecture.title: One platform, three anchor sectors, one bounded control loop.

layers.title: Recovery Node
layers.body: A sector-specific interface combines power conversion, measurement, sensors, isolation, and a local controller.

layers.title: Facility Microgrid
layers.body: The port, station, depot, or water facility decides whether energy is used locally, stored, or held in reserve.

layers.title: District Coordination
layers.body: A bounded cluster shares forecasts and availability across facilities without implying a new shared physical cable.

layers.title: ReGenCity OS
layers.body: A recovery-aware digital twin aggregates available flexibility for planning and a future utility interface.

coordinationStory.title: A bounded response, shown as a sequence
coordinationStory.disclaimer: The simulation is illustrative and does not use live telemetry or utility dispatch.

events.title: A grid need is detected
events.body: The coordinator sees a local demand, voltage, price, or congestion signal in the demonstration model.

events.title: Fast storage responds
events.body: Supercapacitors or batteries provide the first bounded response while service reserves remain protected.

events.title: Recovery refills the local system
events.body: Normal rail, port, or water operations refill storage when recoverable energy is available.

events.title: Deferred loads are restored
events.body: The model releases flexible demand gradually after the response window, subject to local limits.

recoverabilityIndex.title: A screening index for where to start
recoverabilityIndex.body: The Urban Recoverability Index ranks candidate assets before detailed engineering. It combines recoverable energy, cycle frequency, power value, retrofit effort, service criticality, ownership, location, and safety review.
criteria: retrofit effort and remaining equipment life
ownership, data access, and safety requirements

methodologyTeaser.title: What this demonstration does and does not claim
methodologyTeaser.body: The interface explains a system pattern and exposes screening assumptions. It is not a live control room, a fabrication drawing, a financial offer, or a guarantee of site output.

index.title: Explore the recovery nodes
index.body: Each concept uses the same interaction pattern: inspect the model, select a numbered hotspot, change camera or service state, and review the screening assumption.

nodes.name: ReGenPort
nodes.summary: Recover electrical energy during controlled crane lowering cycles while cargo handling remains the primary service.

screeningEstimate.label: screening estimate
screeningEstimate.basis: illustrative crane cycle and capture assumption

operatingSequence: nearby lifting or facility loads receive direct energy first
surplus is routed to short-duration storage
stored energy can support a bounded peak response

hotspots.title: Suspended load
hotspots.description: The lowering event is the source of recoverable potential energy; cargo duty remains the hard operational constraint.

hotspots.title: Motor-generator
hotspots.description: The hoist drive operates regeneratively during a controlled lowering cycle.

hotspots.title: Controlled transmission
hotspots.description: A conceptual transmission and brake path keeps the lowering motion controllable and serviceable.

hotspots.title: DC link and converter
hotspots.description: Bidirectional power electronics condition recovered energy for local loads or storage.

hotspots.title: Supercapacitor rack
hotspots.description: Short-duration storage can absorb repeated high-power pulses before energy is routed onward.

hotspots.title: Battery rack
hotspots.description: A battery path can hold surplus energy for a later local response; chemistry and rating require site study.

hotspots.title: Local edge controller
hotspots.description: Local logic protects voltage, storage limits, isolation, and emergency shutdown without relying on a cloud connection.

hotspots.title: Service isolation
hotspots.description: Isolation and access points keep maintenance separate from the cargo path.

assumptions.statement: Crane duty and cycle profile are illustrative.
assumptions.label: provisional assumption

assumptions.statement: Power-electronics ratings and mechanical interfaces require engineering review.
assumptions.label: provisional assumption

assumptions.statement: The gravity option is a short-duration reserve concept, not a city-scale battery.
assumptions.label: provisional assumption

nodes.name: ReGenTransit
nodes.summary: Capture regenerative braking energy at a wayside node for another train, a station load, or short-duration storage.

screeningEstimate.label: screening estimate
screeningEstimate.basis: illustrative braking profile and capture assumption

operatingSequence: another accelerating train or station load receives energy first
dispatch is bounded by rail safety and service reliability

hotspots.title: Rail vehicle
hotspots.description: The train supplies recoverable energy during normal braking; the system does not add braking events for generation.

hotspots.title: Traction motor
hotspots.description: The traction system operates as a generator during a braking event.

hotspots.title: Traction power interface
hotspots.description: Recovered DC energy returns through the rail power interface toward a local load or wayside converter.

hotspots.title: Wayside converter
hotspots.description: A bidirectional converter conditions the braking energy for storage or direct local use.

hotspots.title: Wayside storage rack
hotspots.description: A supercapacitor, flywheel, or battery path can hold energy between braking and the next useful demand.

hotspots.title: Station load feeder
hotspots.description: Station services can receive recovered energy when a nearby train cannot use it immediately.

hotspots.title: Protection and isolation panel
hotspots.description: Local protection and isolation preserve rail safety and keep the recovery system serviceable.

hotspots.title: Local rail controller
hotspots.description: The controller coordinates storage and load priority while timetable, passenger, and safety constraints remain authoritative.

assumptions.statement: Braking frequency, train mass, and station load are illustrative.
assumptions.label: provisional assumption

assumptions.statement: Wayside location and rail interface require operator and safety review.
assumptions.label: provisional assumption

assumptions.statement: Regenerative braking is an established category; cross-sector coordination is the proposed novelty.
assumptions.label: provisional framing

nodes.name: ReGenFlow
nodes.summary: Recover a portion of hydraulic energy through a serviceable turbine-generator skid while maintaining required pressure and bypass capability.

screeningEstimate.label: screening estimate
screeningEstimate.basis: illustrative hydraulic duty and capture assumption

operatingSequence: pressure reduction is identified at a suitable line or outlet
the turbine-generator recovers part of the hydraulic head
the bypass protects service continuity during maintenance or abnormal conditions
local generation supports the facility or charges storage

hotspots.title: Pipe inlet
hotspots.description: The inlet brings the existing flow to a recovery skid; water service remains the primary duty.

hotspots.title: Isolation valve
hotspots.description: Isolation makes inspection and maintenance possible without relying on the generator path.

hotspots.title: Service bypass
hotspots.description: A bypass preserves flow and pressure when the recovery train is unavailable.

hotspots.title: Pump-as-turbine
hotspots.description: A suitable pump-as-turbine or microturbine converts part of the available hydraulic head.

hotspots.title: Generator
hotspots.description: The rotating machine produces electricity for local use or storage.

hotspots.title: Flow and pressure instrumentation
hotspots.description: Sensors verify operating conditions and help the controller preserve the required pressure band.

hotspots.title: Control cabinet
hotspots.description: Local controls manage converter state, alarms, isolation, and safe fallback.

hotspots.title: Service drain and access
hotspots.description: Drain and access provisions keep the skid serviceable without compromising the live network.

assumptions.statement: Flow, pressure, elevation, and seasonal duty are illustrative.
assumptions.label: provisional assumption

assumptions.statement: Bypass, water quality, and utility protection require a hydraulic study.
assumptions.label: provisional assumption

assumptions.statement: The recovery train must fail safe and preserve water service.
assumptions.label: provisional design principle

methodology.title: Methodology and assumptions
methodology.intro: This build is a communication and interaction prototype. Screening values make the concept comparable across nodes; they are not measurements, procurement specifications, or a field operating plan.

assumptions.title: Demo values are screening values
assumptions.body: Annual energy and flexible-power figures are selected to make the prototype legible. They require site data, metering, and engineering validation before any investment decision.
assumptions.label: provisional assumption

assumptions.title: Primary service is protected
assumptions.body: Cargo throughput, train service and safety, water pressure, and equipment protection remain hard constraints. Recovery is opportunistic and cannot justify wasteful motion.
assumptions.label: provisional design principle

assumptions.title: Safety remains local
assumptions.body: Emergency shutdown, isolation, voltage protection, and safe fallback must work at the equipment or facility layer without cloud availability.
assumptions.label: provisional design principle

assumptions.title: Power and energy are separate
assumptions.body: Recovery nodes may deliver high short-duration power while storing modest energy. The platform is positioned for high-cycle recovery and flexibility, not multi-hour city backup.
assumptions.label: provisional framing

assumptions.title: Site study is required
assumptions.body: Equipment ratings, dimensions, flow and pressure, rail interfaces, tariff treatment, interconnection, maintenance, and structural conditions remain open engineering questions.
assumptions.label: provisional assumption

home.title: Recover what the city already moves.
home.body: A concept demonstration for turning wasted motion, braking, and pressure into locally useful energy and bounded grid flexibility.

microcopy.localFirst: Local use first; storage and dispatch follow.
microcopy.primaryService: Primary service remains the hard constraint.
microcopy.gravityNotice: Short-duration reserve concept — not a city-scale battery.

judgeAnswers.question: Why not use batteries alone?
judgeAnswers.answer: ReGenCity captures energy that already exists, uses it locally where possible, and can reduce the number of high-power cycles placed on batteries.

judgeAnswers.question: Can it generate whenever the grid needs power?
judgeAnswers.answer: Recovery is opportunistic. Automatic response comes from stored energy and flexible loads that normal operations have refilled.

judgeAnswers.question: What is new here?
judgeAnswers.answer: The proposed novelty is a standardized, recovery-first architecture that forecasts, measures, and coordinates established recovery technologies across port, transit, and water systems.
